_comment: Copy to config.json and edit. config.json is gitignored.
_comment_credentials: Both optional but strongly recommended. An NCBI API key raises the Entrez rate limit from 3 to 10 requests/second (https://ncbiinsights.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2017/11/02/new-api-keys-for-the-e-utilities/). The email is required by Unpaywall and puts CrossRef and NCBI requests in their polite pools. Prefer the PUBMED_API_KEY and UNPAYWALL_EMAIL environment variables if you would rather not keep them in a file.
_comment_retmax: Maximum PMIDs fetched from one search. The author query is deliberately broad (it wildcards the initials, because PubMed always indexes 'Surname Initials' but only sometimes indexes 'Surname Forename'), so a common surname can match thousands. If the hit count exceeds this, the tool warns and - when affiliation_keywords are set - narrows the query server-side rather than silently truncating.
_comment_identity: Author disambiguation. This is what stops a search for a common name from returning several different researchers' papers. A name match must additionally satisfy one of: ORCID, email domain, or an affiliation keyword. List every way the institution is written in PubMed affiliation strings, including abbreviations, affiliated hospitals and translated forms - PubMed does not normalise these.

affiliation_keywords: Affiliated Hospital of Example Medical University
author_identity._comment_orcid: Strongest signal available. If you know the target researcher's ORCID, fill it in - it alone resolves most ambiguity.
author_identity._comment_require: true = strict. A name match that satisfies none of the three checks is rejected. Set false to keep every name match (only sensible for genuinely rare names).

_comment_advisor: Read only by the `profile` subcommand; both keys are optional and these are the defaults. The profile report refuses to run unless author_identity above carries at least one of orcid / affiliation_keywords / email_domains, because without them the corpus blends several same-named people and every count in the report is about more than one person.

advisor._comment_exclude_names: Co-authors to drop from the roster, written exactly as PubMed indexes them ('Surname Forename'). Intended for a co-PI, a department head or a long-term collaborator who appears on everything and would otherwise be counted as a member of this lab. Matching is case-insensitive and exact - it is not a keyword search.
advisor._comment_lag_years: How long someone must have been publishing before 'no first-author paper yet' means anything. Below this, they are reported as too recent to tell rather than as having never led a paper, so a lab that just expanded does not read as one that withholds first authorship.
